items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: There is the Fats Waller version, the Art Tatum version, the Bud Powell version, the Nat King Cole version, the Oscar Peterson version.

ctx.x: Well said. You made me feel lighter yesterday when I was listening to “St. Louis Blues.”

By the way, “St. Louis Blues” has been one of those tunes that Earl Hines had the wonderful rendition of that tune, and one of those tunes that became a tour de force for piano players you know. Even Willie “The Lion” Smith, the great stride piano player, he said that the greatest tune ever written was the “St. Louis Blues.” Tommy Flanagan even recorded the “St. Louis Blues.” So that’s one of those tunes, like another one for example is “Tea for Two” — that all the great piano players, they came up with a signed…
I love that kind of composition that just has something that attracts it. When I play that tune I love the — I guess it’s the first 8 bars going into the second 8, that harmonic transition is so hip.
